newsitem.title: FRANCE: SNCF still needs "some weeks" for telecom deal.
newsitem.headline: SNCF still needs "some weeks" for telecom deal.

text.p: French railways company SNCF said it still needed a few weeks to decide on an industrial partner to run its telecommunications network.
"This decision is too important to be dealt with quickly. We will make an announcement in the next few weeks," an SNCF spokesman said.
The company had been expected to make a decision at the start of the year after having asked the bidding parties to refine their offers in late November.
Cegetel, a joint venture of Generale des Eaux, British Telecom Plc, Germany's Mannesmann and SBC Communications Inc, is one of the parties.
Bouygues and Italy's STET form another team while U.S. group AT&T and Unisource have also made a bid.
Unisource is a joint venture of Dutch PTT, Telia of Sweden, Swiss Telecom PTT and Spain's Telefonica.
The network of SNCF's Telecom Developpement currently has 8,000 km of fibre optic cable which it will increase to 11,000 to 12,000 km in three to four years.

The backbone of the SNCF network could be an important element in any so-called "alternative network" for a telecoms group aiming to compete with France Telecom when the market is liberalised in 1998.
In Germany, Mannesmann on Thursday finalised a deal with AT&T and Unisource to set up a new telecom company with the network of railways Deutsche Bahn AG.
A spokesman for the SNCF said the German decision did not have any influence on the choice of the French group.
